en: Refers to the process in which a needle and thread or fine wire are used to stitch decorative designs into cloth, leather, paper, or other material. It may also refer to the process used to create machine-made imitations of hand-made embroidery. For the weft patterning technique of weaving raised patterns on a woven textile, use  brocading  (AAT).

Hue name for one of the three primary subtractive colors. Represents that portion of the spectrum lying between green and orange, with a wavelength range between 565 and 590 nanometers. The term may refer to any of this group of colors that vary in lightness and saturation. Examples of yellow color in nature are that of a ripe lemon and the yolk of an egg (AAT)

UCL (Universal Color Language) standard color name identifying whitish colors, such as the color of snow or milk. More specifically, white is the absence of color. It is the color produced by reflection, transmission, or emission of all kinds of light in the proportion in which they exist in the complete visible spectrum, without sensible absorption, being thus fully luminous and devoid of any distinctive hue (AAT)
Hue name for any color intermediate between black and white, or composed of a mixture of black and white with little or no positive hue (AAT)

Hue name for the color representing that portion of the spectrum that is intermediate between red and yellow, with wavelengths between 585 and 620 nanometers. The term may refer to any of this group of colors that vary in lightness and saturation. An example of orange color in nature is that of the citrus fruit orange, for which the color is named in modern English. It is a secondary pigment color (made by combining yellow and red) (AAT)

en: White-to-yellowish seed-hair fibers of several species of the genus Gossypium, native to most subtropical areas of the world; used especially for making textile, cord, padding, rag paper, and for cellulose used for plastic and rayon (AAT).

A waxy, odorous substance of marbled ashy color produced in the intestines of the sperm whale, and often found floating in tropical seas, or on the seashore. Formerly used as an ingredient in perfumery to prevent evaporation, more recently it has been replaced in this function by synthetic substances (AAT).

Hue name for one of the three primary additive colors; that portion of the spectrum lying at the lowest frequencies of light discernible by the human eye, with a wavelength range between 630 and 760 nanometers. The term may refer to any of this group of colors that vary in lightness and saturation. Examples of red color in nature are that of blood and ripe cherries (AAT)

The huipil is a simple rectangular, sleeveless garment that covers the shoulders and part of the arms and may fall to the hips in length, but reaches to the ankles elsewhere. In Mixtec, the huipil is also called 'Shiku lestu'. Wearing it expresses many aspects of social life. \Normally, a huipil consists of three separate strips that are put together to form a huipil. However, this huipil consists of two strips made of white factory cotton, one strip of 77 cm wide and a right strip of 19 cm wide. Vertical embroidered flowers in the colors blue, yellow, red, pink and orange suggest that the huipil consists of three separate strips. The side of the huipil is sewn shut with a small opening at the top that serves as armholes. The sides are finished with vertical floral motifs in the same colors. The round neckline is finished with grey cotton ribbon, cut in triangle shapes. Both on the front and the back of the huipil there is a large flower embroidered below the neckline in the colors blue, red, yellow, orange and pink. At the Mixteca, the flower motif represent the feminine. \Description Christensen:Commercial white cotton, commercial yarn used for embroideryAcquired 1966 in Igualapa, Gro.  \Description:Garment consists of two pieces of commercial white cotton. One is 77 cm wide, the other, forming the right side of the garment, is 19 cm wide, with a separate piece (12 x 19 cm) at the hem. Vertical embroidered bands of floral designs in multi-coloured commercial cotton yarn create suggestion of a three-panel huipil. Below neck opening, on front and back, are embroidered large multi-coloured floral designs. The circular neck opening has a finish of grey cotton ribbon, cut in star shape. \It is worn with gathered skirt with flounces of commercial cotton.

nl:
De huipil is een eenvoudig rechthoekig, mouwloos kledingstuk dat de schouders en een deel van de armen bedekt en in de lengte tot op de heupen kan vallen, maar elders tot aan de enkels reikt. In het Mixteeks wordt de huipil ook wel ‘Shiku lestu’ genoemd. Met het dragen ervan worden vele aspecten van het sociale leven tot uiting gebracht. 
Normaal gesproken bestaat een huipil uit drie losse banen die aan elkaar worden gezet tot een huipil. Deze huipil bestaat echter uit twee banen gemaakt van wit fabriekskatoen, een baan van 77 cm breed en een rechterbaan van 19 cm breed. Verticale geborduurde bloemen motief in de kleuren blauw- geel- rood- roze en oranje maakt de suggestie dat de huipil wel uit drie losse banen bestaat. De zijkant van de huipil is dicht genaaid met een kleine opening aan de bovenkant, die als armgaten dient. De zijkanten zijn afgewerkt met verticaal lopende bloemmotieven in dezelfde kleuren. De ronde hals is afgewerkt met grijs lint gemaakt van katoen, uitgesneden in driehoekvormen. Zowel op de voor als de achterkant van de huipil is onder de hals een grote bloem geborduurd in de kleuren blauw- rood- geel- oranje en roze. Bij de Mixteca staan het bloem motief voor het vrouwelijke. 

Beschrijving Christensen:
Commercial white cotton, commercial yarn used for embroidery
Acquired 1966 in Igualapa, Gro.  
Description: Garment consists of two pieces of commercial white cotton. One is 77 cm wide, the other, forming the right side of the garment, is 19 cm wide, with a separate piece (12 x 19 cm) at the hem. Vertical embroidered bands of floral designs in multi-coloured commercial cotton yarn create suggestion of a three-panel huipil. Below neck opening, on front and back, are embroidered large multi-coloured floral designs. The circular neck opening has a finish of grey cotton ribbon, cut in star shape. 

Used with gathered skirt with flounces of commercial cotton.

Provenience: Yoloxochitl, Mun. of San Luis Acatlán, Gro.
